cases.given: A UI error label and recovery action must be written to match verified behavior.
expect: Activate Scribe and load interface-text guidance.
Keep the problem, available recovery, terminology, and runtime contract aligned.
Use available interface and engineering guardrails without making them prerequisites for Scribe.

cases.given: A proposed decision record needs a clear technical choice, consequences, and revisit condition.
expect: Do not activate Scribe for the domain owner's normal Decision record.
Preserve the record's canonical format owner and required rationale fields.
Add Scribe only when substantive wording or fidelity is independently requested.

cases.given: A structured project work item already supplies its format's exact outcome, acceptance, evidence, and next-action fields and only needs format-preserving insertion.
expect: Do not activate Scribe or load the continuous-prose reference.
Preserve the canonical labels, order, and supplied wording.
Do not narrate Skill routing or reference selection.

cases.given: A documentation edit has no project plan, decision-record format, or sibling Scoville Skills installed.
expect: Apply Scribe normally from the supplied facts and documentation conventions.
Do not create a plan or decision record and do not require a sibling Skill.
Verify the edited meaning and report only material unresolved facts.

cases.given: Three coherent proposed decision records need explicit user lifecycle choices.
expect: Do not activate Scribe for the domain owner's normal proposal report.
Report the three proposals once as one compact set.
Include each record's identifier or title and practical effect.
Ask for the required user choices without assuming one fixed lifecycle or repeating setup narration.

cases.given: Summarize a retry change from 240 milliseconds and 8 attempts to 120 milliseconds and 16 attempts as change, expected effect, and remaining risk. Functional tests pass, but CPU cost on very large pages is unmeasured.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Fidelity summary guidance plus Prose when explanatory quality is variable.
State that the maximum retry window remains exactly 1.92 seconds rather than implying that it became longer.
Separate the denser retry cadence and faster possible detection from the unmeasured CPU risk.

cases.given: Write 70 to 90 words from three allowed services while treating company age, guarantees, awards, fixed delivery times, and service area as unsupported facts.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Prose guidance.
Use only the allowed services and introduce no unsupported quality claim.
Keep the negative source constraints out of the visible service copy rather than restating them as a disclaimer or process note.

cases.given: Explain what makes a language model useful to a technically sophisticated user despite errors and lack of first-hand experience, naming both capabilities and clear limits.
expect: Do not activate Scribe or load Prose for an ordinary technical explanation.
Account for both requested dimensions before concluding: useful capabilities and clear limits.
Keep the quality checks under the host system prompt rather than treating the explanation as a reusable artifact.

cases.given: Write a customer-facing announcement in chat for later copying and publication.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Prose guidance.
Treat explicit reuse and publication intent as artifact signals even though delivery is in chat.
Use only permitted facts and produce copy-ready prose.

cases.given: Review a patch for correctness and return actionable findings without drafting a separate publication artifact.
expect: Do not activate Scribe.
Keep implementation evidence and findings under the engineering owner.
Do not add Scribe merely because findings use prose.

cases.given: After drafting an announcement, first shorten it while preserving every claim, then explain why one qualifier had to remain.
expect: Reactivate Scribe with Prose and Fidelity for the follow-up transformation.
Do not carry Scribe into the later ordinary explanation.
Classify the two segments independently.

cases.given: Draft a short customer announcement in English and German. The service will be unavailable on Friday from 18:00 to 19:00 for maintenance. No other facts are available.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Prose guidance.
Use no em dashes, en dashes, or semicolons in either language.
Prefer complete sentences and ordinary punctuation. Use an ASCII hyphen as a sentence-level dash only when needed, not as a recurring construction.
Preserve the maintenance time and introduce no unsupported claims.

cases.given: Edit this announcement for clarity while preserving its claims: The update is ready—it fixes the export error; installation is optional. The read-only preview remains available–no installation is needed to use it.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Prose guidance.
Remove em dashes, en dashes, and semicolons from the editable prose without replacing each one with a single or double hyphen.
Preserve the necessary hyphen in read-only, every claim, and the optional installation condition.
Keep the edit narrow and the wording natural.

cases.given: Rewrite this interface error using only the verified behavior that export failed and Retry starts another export attempt: Export failed—your file was not created; select Retry to try again.
expect: Activate Scribe and load Interface guidance, without loading Prose solely for punctuation rules.
Use no em dashes, en dashes, or semicolons in the rewritten error.
Preserve the canonical Retry label and describe only the supported recovery action.

cases.given: Write a short documentation paragraph containing this exact quotation: Ready—not released; wait for approval. Include this command unchanged: echo ready; echo done. Preserve the exact URL https://example.com/a;b and the canonical name North–South. Add one explanatory sentence stating that release approval is still required.
expect: Activate Scribe with Fidelity for the exact quotation and Prose for the variable surrounding paragraph.
Preserve the quotation, command, URL, and canonical name exactly, including their punctuation.
Use no em dashes, en dashes, or semicolons in the newly written explanatory prose.
Keep fixed-insertion and Source-exact content unchanged when the same protected text is requested through either mode.

cases.given: Write a disposable draft but explicitly do not use Scoville Scribe.
expect: Load no Scribe Core or reference.
Use the host's compact fallback behavior.
Keep the opt-out local to the current task.
